title: Deep Generative Models for Synthetic Data: A Survey
authors: Eigenschink, P.; Reutterer, T.; Vamosi, S.; Vamosi, R.; Sun, C.; Kalcher, K.
tldr: Proposes data-driven evaluation framework for synthetic sequential data with five criteria: representativeness, novelty, realism, diversity, and coherence across NLP, healthcare, mobility, and audio domains.
problem_and_motivation: Deep generative models for synthetic data have become specialized and disconnected across domains. No unified evaluation framework exists for comparing synthetic data quality across different architectures and applications.
approach: Proposes five-criteria evaluation framework: representativeness, novelty, realism, diversity, and coherence.
Reviews generative models for sequential data across NLP, speech, audio, healthcare, and mobility domains.
Examines GANs, VAEs, autoregressive models, and flow-based models.
Analyzes evaluation metrics used for each criterion across domains.
findings: Realism and coherence more important for NLP, speech, and audio synthetic data.
Novelty and representativeness more important for healthcare and mobility synthetic data.
Representativeness measured using statistical metrics, realism by human judgment, novelty by privacy tests.
GANs receive most attention among generative architectures for sequential data.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Provides a unified evaluation framework for synthetic sequential data independent of model architecture. Identifies which quality criteria matter most in different application domains.
directly_justifies: Synthetic data quality must be evaluated on multiple criteria beyond statistical similarity.
Privacy concerns drive synthetic data adoption in healthcare and finance.
limits: Focuses on sequential data; does not comprehensively cover image or tabular data.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 topic domains. Flagged 14.A (high), 10.A (high), 6.B (medium). Rejected 1.A-5.C, 7.A-13.C as outside scope.

limitations: Survey limited to sequential data types.
Evaluation framework proposed but not empirically validated. [unacknowledged]
remember_this: Five-criteria framework: representativeness, novelty, realism, diversity, coherence.
Privacy protection is a key driver for synthetic data adoption.
